newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hilasal sees higher sales for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hilasal sees higher sales for 1996.

text.p: Towel-maker Hilasal, which recently went public, expects sales to grow by 36.5 percent in 1996 over 1995, company director general Jorge Garcia Fernandez said Friday.
"It's a projection of growth ... in terms of units sold," Garcia told Reuters in an interview.
Hilasal expects sales of 2.96 million units this year compared to 2.168 million units sold last year, when Hilasel controlled 62 percent of the Mexican market, Garcia said.
The company expects to export 40 percent of its production to 80 countries, he said.
In 1997, Hilasal expects to increase capacity by 64 percent in order to make greater inroads into the tourist industry, he said.
In June, Hilasal issued stock equal to 27.71 percent of its capital on the Mexican stock exchange.
